# MiniMax H3 Workflow Refactor

> **Design philosophy:** The user should control meaningful settings, while the workflow handles the internal routing, dependencies, and consequences automatically.

---

## Instructions

- Use the **Control Panel** for the main workflow settings.
- Set your resolution, duration, FPS, reference counts, and feature toggles there.
- The workflow will handle the internal routing automatically based on those controls.

### References

Set the number of references being used from the Control Panel:

- **Images:** 0–6
- **Audio:** 0–3
- **Video:** 0–2

Reference inputs are always enabled **sequentially from the first slot onward**.

For example:

- `1` image reference uses `<Picture 1>`
- `2` image references use `<Picture 1>` and `<Picture 2>`
- `3` image references use `<Picture 1>`, `<Picture 2>`, and `<Picture 3>`

The same rule applies to audio and video references.

You cannot select arbitrary reference slots with the count controls. If you want to use a specific set of references, place them in the first available slots in the order you want them used.

You do not need to manually bypass individual reference groups.

### Video Continuation

- Enable **Video Continuation** from the Control Panel.
- Load the source video in the continuation section.
- Set **OG Video Has Audio** correctly.
- Choose the desired overlap length.
- **Single Pass is no longer required.**
- **Final Upscale can be used with Video Continuation.**
- When Final Upscale is enabled, the completed stitched video is upscaled/refined as a whole.

### Final Upscale

- Be mindful of your GPU when using **Final Upscale**, especially with long videos or higher resolutions.
- Upscaling the full stitched result can significantly increase VRAM usage and processing time.
- For longer generations, you may need to reduce resolution, duration, or disable Final Upscale depending on your available VRAM.

### Force Audio

- Enable **Force Audio** from the Control Panel.
- Choose whether Force Audio should use:
  - `<Audio 1>`
  - `<Video 1>` embedded audio
- Enable **Trim Duration to Audio** if you want the generation duration to follow the selected audio source.

---

## Fixed

- Fixed Final Upscale so it uses the actual generated result
- Fixed Video Continuation so the full stitched video can be upscaled
- Fixed continuation audio routing so there is only one valid audio path
- Fixed the old dependency between Video Continuation and Single Pass

---

## Improved

- Improved the workflow control logic so users control features instead of bypass states
- Improved Video Continuation, including stitching, audio handling, and compatibility with Final Upscale
- Improved reference handling with direct image, audio, and video reference counts
- Improved overall state management with centralized controls and named `Set` / `Get` values
- Improved the Final Upscale path so video and audio are handled correctly through the second pass

---

## Added

- Added a centralized control panel
- Added direct reference-count controls
- Added support for using `<Video 1>` audio with Force Audio
- Added **Trim Duration to Audio**
- Added global FPS control
- Added whole-video upscale after continuation stitching

nodes.title: Prompt Templates/Examples
widgets_values:
.: V2V Editing (replace a character in a target video) --- NOTE: TENDS TO LOOK BETTER ON SINGLE PASS. SEE OPTION ABOVE ---

subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the girl whose motion comes from <Video 1> and whose appearance comes from <Picture 1>.
<Video 1> is the source video for the target video edit.

summary:
[video editing + reference generation] The target video is an edited version of <Video 1>. The girl's appearance is styled from <Picture 1>. Her motion, camera movement, background, and lighting from the video are preserved continuously from start to finish without deviation at any point.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears throughout [Shot 1]): partially_preserved - the girl's face, body proportions, and skin tone from <Picture 1> are retained, and her motion, choreography, rhythm, and timing from <Video 1> are retained at every moment. 
<Video 1> (whole-video temporal structure, motion path, camera movement, background, lighting): fully_preserved - the girl's choreography, movement speed, gestures, body positions, camera framing, camera movement, background, and lighting from every frame of <Video 1> are preserved throughout the entire target video without deviation.

detailed_description:
The target video uses a naturalistic style matching the source footage, preserving its original lighting, color grading, and camera work.
[Shot 1] The camera follows <Subject 1>, the girl, as she exists in the same setting from <Video 1>. Her appearance matches <Picture 1> — same skin tone, body shape, and natural contours. Throughout the entire video, her motion is a frame-by-frame motion match to <Video 1>: the same choreography, gestures, limb positions, movement speed, and rhythm are followed continuously from start to finish. The camera framing, angle, and movement stay locked to <Video 1> at all times. The background remains identical and unchanged.


.: Reference Generation (general filmmaking):

subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the character in <Picture 1>. (basic description)

<Subject 2> is the scene location in <Picture 2>. (basic scene description)

summary:
[reference generation + audio reference] highly realistic live-action scene of <Subject 1> in <Subject 2>.

retention_analysis:
<Audio 1>: reference - its vocal timbre guides the vocal delivery of <Subject 1> without copying the original signal.

detailed_description:
[Shot 1]: a close up shot of <Subject 1> with a shocked expression as the camera pulls in towards her face. Suddenly, she turns around to look behind her.
[Shot 2]: a 3/4ths shot of <Subject 1> as she turns, her expression is confused. She tilts her head to one side, a look of questioning. She hesitantly says using <Audio 1> as her vocal-timbre reference: <d>[English]Hello?.. Is anyone there?</d> her tone is hesitant and suspicious.
[Shot 3]: an over-the-shoulder following shot as <Subject 1> begins to walk through <Subject 2> looking around side to side.
 
overall_soundscape:
interior ambience.

non_diegetic_music:
N/A

widgets_values:
subject_definitions:
<Picture 2> is the reference image providing the appearance of <Subject 1>.
<Audio 1> is the voice reference providing the vocal timbre, tone, cadence, and speaking characteristics of <Subject 1>.
<Subject 1> is the woman whose appearance comes from <Picture 2> and whose voice comes from <Audio 1>, preserving her recognizable facial features, hairstyle, skin tone, eye shape, makeup, clothing, overall visual identity, and vocal character.

<Picture 3> is the reference image providing the appearance of <Subject 2>.
<Subject 2> is the person whose appearance comes from <Picture 3>, preserving her recognizable facial features, hairstyle, skin tone, eye shape, clothing, and overall visual identity.


summary:
[reference generation] A highly realistic live-action 5-second video inside a dark movie theater immediately after a movie has ended. <Subject 1> sits beside <Subject 2>, who is seated in the chair directly to her left. Everyone in the theater, including <Subject 2>, continuously claps in enthusiastic applause throughout the entire clip except for <Subject 1>. <Subject 1> stares at <Subject 2> until exactly 00:04.000, then speaks directly to her and asks, "How old are you supposed to be? Like.... 12?" The applause continues uninterrupted and nobody reacts.


retention_analysis:
<Picture 2>: fully_preserved - the reference image provides the visual identity and appearance of <Subject 1>.

<Audio 1>: reference - its vocal timbre, tone, cadence, and speaking characteristics guide the vocal delivery of <Subject 1>.

<Subject 1> (appears throughout [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - her facial structure, hairstyle, skin tone, makeup, clothing, and overall visual identity from <Picture 2> remain consistent throughout the video. Her vocal delivery is guided by <Audio 1>.

<Picture 3>: fully_preserved - the reference image provides the visual identity and appearance of <Subject 2>.

<Subject 2> (appears throughout [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - her facial structure, hairstyle, skin tone, clothing, and overall visual identity from <Picture 3> remain consistent throughout the video.


detailed_description:
The video uses highly realistic cinematic live-action photography with natural skin texture, realistic facial expressions, accurate body movement, and believable low-light movie-theater illumination.

[Shot 1] <Subject 1> and <Subject 2> are seated next to each other in padded movie-theater chairs. <Subject 2> is in the chair directly to <Subject 1>'s left. <Subject 1> is looking at <Subject 2> with contempt.

The camera faces them from the row in front at approximately eye level in a medium shot that clearly shows both subjects, their upper bodies, their hands, and part of their theater seats.

The movie has just ended. From the very beginning of the video through the final frame, the entire theater audience continuously applauds. <Subject 2> continuously claps along with the rest of the audience for the entire clip while smiling like a stupid bimbo. The surrounding audience also continuously claps for the entire clip. The applause never stops or pauses at any point.

<Subject 2> is looking directly ahead.

<Subject 1> does not clap and is looking at subject one with contempt, disgust, and confusion.

At 00:04.000, <Subject 1> (S1) says directly to <Subject 2> using <Audio 1> as her vocal-timbre reference, <d>[English] How old are you even supposed to be?</d>
 while <Subject 2> and the audience in the background continue to clap.

<Subject 2> glances at <Subject 1> and then back to the front while continuing to smile and clap like an idiot.

The audience and <Subject 2> continue to applaud.


overall_soundscape:
Continuous enthusiastic applause from the entire theater throughout the full video.

<Subject 1>'s dialogue uses <Audio 1> as the voice reference and is clearly audible over the applause.


non_diegetic_music:
N/A

nodes.title: CUSTOM NODE LINKS
widgets_values:
.: Load Image Node
https://github.com/obvpm/comfyui-obvpm (must be manually installed, unzipped folder into /custom_nodes/)

.: Latent Upscaler
- Node: https://github.com/LBH-123-AI/Comfyui_Minimax_h3_latent_Upscaler
- Latent Upscale Model: https://huggingface.co/LBH-123-AI/Minimax_h3_latent_Upscaler/blob/main/minimax_h3_latent_upscaler_3d_bf16.safetensors
(put into /latent_upscale_models/ folder)

.: Sparse Attention 
https://github.com/Zironic/H3-Optimizations

.: Prompt IDE
https://github.com/ethanfel/ComfyUI-H3-Prompt-IDE

.: Turbo LoRA (not recommended to use for high quality production, but for 2d/3d/fun they're ok)
https://huggingface.co/lightx2v/Minimax-h3-Turbo/blob/main/minimax_h3_fl2v_turbo_8step_v1.0_768p_comfyui_bf16.safetensors
Lightx2v's recommendation is to use euler/beta, with shift value 6.0/3.0

.: Audio/Video Loader node
https://github.com/WhatDreamsCost/WhatDreamsCost-ComfyUI

.: Kijai's int8 Video VAE (much faster than default!)
https://huggingface.co/Kijai/MiniMax-H3-experimental/blob/main/minimax_h3_video_vae_int8_convrot.safetensors

.: TaeH3 (for Kijai's Model Preview Override):
https://huggingface.co/Kijai/MiniMax-H3-TAE/blob/main/vae_approx/taeh3.safetensors

Everything else should be easily available from the ComfyUI-manager Install Missing Nodes screen!

-------------------------------

Download the Node-pack zip files and extract into:
ComfyUI_windows_portable\ComfyUI\custom_nodes\ folder.

Or if you have git installed, go into custom_nodes folder and open CMD prompt and type:
git clone [url]
